reason: The text depicts multiple regular human characters exercising clear agency. Isaac prays to God for his wife's fertility (וַיְהִי יִצְחָק בֶּן־ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה... וַיֶּעְתַּר יִצְחָק לַֽיהוָה), Rebekah inquires of God when troubled by her pregnancy (וַתֹּאמֶר אִם־ כֵּן... וַתֵּלֶךְ לִדְרֹשׁ אֶת־ יְהוָֽה), Jacob prepares food and initiates a transaction (וַיָּזֶד יַעֲקֹב נָזִיד... וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב מִכְרָה... אֶת־ בְּכֹֽרָתְךָ לִֽי), and Esau negotiates and makes a deliberate choice to sell his birthright (וַיִּמְכֹּר אֶת־ בְּכֹרָתוֹ לְיַעֲקֹֽב). These are portrayed as ordinary family members with distinct personalities, professions, and the capacity to make consequential decisions.
